approach_variants.name: Elbow Lake Trail and the Green Creek path to the low notch on the Cinderella-Little Sister ridge
approach_variants.season: Roughly Jul-Sep
approach_variants.notes:
Start at the Elbow Lake Trailhead (Trail #697) at the end of FS Road 38. The trail immediately meets the Middle Fork Nooksack — there is no bridge at the marked crossing, and fording can be dangerous or impassable at high water. Many parties use an unofficial log crossing roughly a quarter mile downstream of the official ford, made of logs lashed between two boulders.

Once across, climb through forest about 1.5 miles to a switchback near Hildebrand Creek, where the unmaintained, blue-blazed Green Creek Climber's Trail splits LEFT into the Green Creek cirque. Look closely for the small blue markers; it is easy to walk past.

Follow it up into the basin — Green Creek runs clear and is a reliable water source along this stretch. Above treeline the trail gives way to talus and boulder fields and then loose, unstable scree, with Class 3 rock steps to reach the toe of the Green Creek (Sisters) Glacier. Route-finding through that section is the crux of the approach.

Cross the low-angle glacier to the low notch on the ridge between Cinderella and Little Sister.

Most parties treat this as a multi-day trip, camping near Elbow Lake or in the Green Creek basin.
approach_variants.baseFinding:
THE LOW NOTCH ON THE CINDERELLA-LITTLE SISTER RIDGE IS THE BASE, AND IT IS WHERE YOU STOW GLACIER GEAR. Cross the low-angle Green Creek (Sisters) Glacier and step off ice onto rock at the notch. It is a col: a low point with a peak at each end of it, Cinderella one way and Little Sister the other.

THE MOAT AT THE GLACIER MARGIN IS THE LAST OBSTACLE AND IT IS SEASONAL, NOT STRUCTURAL — trivial in a heavy snow year, a real step late in the season, and exactly the same problem in reverse on the way down. Plan for it in both directions rather than being surprised at 4pm.

FROM THE NOTCH, GO WEST, NOT EAST. Cinderella's WEST RIDGE is the route — a long ridge, mostly straightforward walking on broken ground with a short section of enjoyable scrambling to the true summit. Turning the other way out of the notch heads for Little Sister.

DO NOT BE TEMPTED ALONG THE CREST TOWARD LITTLE SISTER. This is documented rather than cautious: at least one account calls that connecting ridgeline a missile zone and recommends dropping back to the glacier from this notch instead of traversing it. The notch serves two peaks and connects neither.

ON THE WEST RIDGE, THE CREST DIRECT IS THE TRAP. Taking it absolutely direct runs into stretches of committing downclimbing; the standard escape is to DROP INTO A GULLY ON THE SOUTH SIDE and regain easier ground above. Committing downclimbing on a Class 3-4 scramble means you have stayed on the crest too long.

THE ROCK IS DUNITE AND IT BEHAVES TWO WAYS AT ONCE, which is the single most useful thing to know about holds here: notably grippy on WEATHERED surfaces, and greasy where a block has FRESHLY BROKEN. Judge each hold on its surface, not on the rock type.
hazards: A bridgeless Middle Fork Nooksack crossing, impassable at high water
An easy-to-miss blue-blazed junction near Hildebrand Creek
Loose unstable scree and Class 3 steps to reach the glacier — the crux of the approach
A moat at the glacier margin in both directions
A connecting ridge toward Little Sister that accounts describe as a missile zone

The row's own approach says the ridge is 'typically reached after climbing the North Face or Hanging Glacier route to the upper mountain, or via the NW Rib', and its approach_logistics repeats that there is no independent start. So the base is a point somewhere on another route, and unlike Stuart's Great Gendarme — a tower that stands up in front of you and cannot be confused with anything — nothing published locates WHERE along the crest a party joins it. Writing a base finding here would be inventing the one fact that matters.

Enriching both would put two approaches and two different base findings on what is probably one climb. The North Ridge row is the one written; see _DEFECTS.

The entire published approach in this row is 'as for the Easton Glacier route, branching onto the Squak Glacier line rather than the Railroad Grade/Easton line; high camp is commonly established around 6,800 ft.' Where the branch happens, and what you would see at it, is exactly what is not stated — and 'branching off somewhere before the moraine' is not a fog test. The peak's base finding is carried by wa_sherman_peak_baker_route, which shares the summit; and wa_mount_baker_squak_glacier already holds variants for the Squak line itself.
_SKIPPED.wa_icy_peak_ruth_icy_traverse: DUPLICATE ROW. wa_icy_peak_ruth_icy_traverse and wa_ruth_icy_traverse describe the same outing — Hannegan Pass, over Ruth, down to the Ruth-Icy saddle, across to the Icy Glacier, up Icy — filed under two different areas with the same 8,000 ft gain. The Ruth-filed row carries far more detail and is the one written. See _DEFECTS.
_SKIPPED.wa_american_border_peak_northeast_face: EMPTY ROW PLUS A LIVE CONTAMINATION RISK, and the two together decided it. The row holds a name, an aspect, a season and a high point and nothing else: no approach, no logistics, no descent, no beta. There is no published Washington-side description of a northeast-face line on this peak to re-home. And the peak's near-twin — CANADIAN Border Peak, about a kilometre north across the international line — does have north-side beta, reached from British Columbia. Writing anything here would mean either inventing a base or importing one from a different country's mountain, which is precisely the failure this catalog has already taken once.
_SKIPPED.wa_north_twin_sister_west_ridge: DUPLICATE ROW. wa_north_twin_sister_west_ridge and wa_north_twin_sister_scramble carry identical gain (5,500 ft), identical distance (9.7 km), identical high point (6,644 ft), the same aspect and the same season, and both describe the west ridge of North Twin. They differ only in grade label (Class 3-4 against Class 3) and in which logging-road approach they name. Rather than write two base findings for one crest, BOTH road approaches were folded into the scramble row as two variants, which is what approach_variants exist for. See _DEFECTS.
_SKIPPED.wa_south_twin_sister_scramble: DUPLICATE ROW. Its approach text says in as many words 'Identical to the West Ridge approach', it shares the West Ridge row's distance (20.1 km) and high point (7,004 ft), and its descent describes the south-side gullies that the West Ridge row already carries as its own alternative finish. It is the West Ridge with a south-gully descent, not a separate line with a separate base.
_SKIPPED.wa_little_sister_west_face: POSITIONED ONLY RELATIVE, AND ITS FIRST ASCENT IS ALREADY ON ANOTHER ROW. The whole published position is 'around to the west side of Little Sister (often linked with Skookum Peak on the circuit)' — a bearing round a mountain, not a marker. Separately, its first ascent (Darin Berdinka, 21 June 2013) is the same one recorded in wa_little_sister_scramble's fa field, annotated there as '(West Face)'. Until that is untangled, writing a west-face base finding risks describing the same climb twice. See _DEFECTS.
_SKIPPED.wa_skookum_peak_twinsisters_scramble: ITS OWN APPROACH CONTRADICTS ITSELF, so there is nothing safe to re-home. The row says to follow Elbow Lake Trail #697 for about 8 miles to Elbow Lake and only then pick up the Green Creek climbers' path. Every other route in this basin — and the sources for all of them — put the Green Creek path leaving #697 at a switchback near Hildebrand Creek around 2,600 ft, roughly 1.5 miles in. Meanwhile the Green Creek Circuit accounts reach Skookum's north ridge by dropping off South Twin's southwest side, not from the Green Creek cirque at all. Two irreconcilable approaches and a base stated only as 'before gaining the ridge'. Reported rather than guessed; see _DEFECTS.

_DEFECTS._note: Data defects noticed in passing while reading these rows. Reported, not fixed — this batch writes only approach_variants.
_DEFECTS.duplicate_lincoln_northwest_face: wa_lincoln_peak_wilkes_booth ('Wilkes-Booth (Northwest Face)', 4p, aspect NW) and wa_lincoln_peak_north_ridge ('North Ridge / Standard', IV WI4, 5p, aspect NW) share an identical first-ascent party AND date — Daniel Coltrane and Michal Rynkiewicz, 13 March 2015 — on the same aspect of the same peak. Two rows, probably one climb. Confirm before either is deleted: the pitch counts differ and only one carries a grade.
_DEFECTS.lincoln_north_ridge_row_contradicts_its_: wa_lincoln_peak_north_ridge's fa column says Coltrane and Rynkiewicz, 13 March 2015. Its own approach prose says the line was 'first climbed in May 1958 (Cooper and O'Conner)'. Both cannot be the first ascent of the same line, and which is right bears directly on whether the Wilkes-Booth row above is a duplicate.
_DEFECTS.lincoln_x_couloir_descent_returns_to_the: wa_lincoln_peak_standard's approach is explicit and correct that the X Couloir is reached from the SOUTH via the Middle Fork Nooksack Road (FR-38) and Rankin Creek, and it warns in as many words that Heliotrope Ridge serves a different line on the peak. Its own descent_text then has the party rope up for a glacier crossing 'back to the Coleman Glacier toe and the Heliotrope Ridge Trail' and reverse the climb 'back to the Thunder Glacier cirque'. The descent walks out to a different trailhead on the other side of the mountain from the one the approach drove to.
_DEFECTS.lincoln_north_ridge_calls_the_x_couloir_: The mirror of the defect above. wa_lincoln_peak_north_ridge's approach says 'where the standard route cuts southwest toward the Thunder Glacier cirque', implying the standard route also starts at Heliotrope. wa_lincoln_peak_standard says it starts at FR-38 and Rankin Creek. The two rows describe the same 'standard route' as starting on opposite sides of the peak.
_DEFECTS.duplicate_ruth_icy_traverse: wa_ruth_icy_traverse (filed under wa_ruth_mountain) and wa_icy_peak_ruth_icy_traverse (filed under wa_icy_peak) both describe the Ruth-to-Icy traverse with the same 8,000 ft of gain. Two rows, one climb, two areas — the same shape as the Sherpa north-ridge pair recorded in the Stuart batch. A third row, wa_icy_peak_southwest_route, describes substantially the same day from the Icy end and is arguably a third copy, though it has enough independent detail about the Icy Glacier and the summit gully to stand alone.
_DEFECTS.duplicate_north_twin_west_ridge: wa_north_twin_sister_west_ridge and wa_north_twin_sister_scramble carry identical gain_ft (5,500), dist_km (9.7), high_point_ft (6,644), aspect and season, and both describe North Twin's west ridge. They disagree only on grade label and on which logging-road approach they name — which suggests one climb imported twice from two sources rather than two routes.
_DEFECTS.three_rows_share_the_name_twin_sisters_o: wa_little_sister_scramble, wa_cinderella_peak_scramble and wa_skookum_peak_twinsisters_scramble are three routes on three different peaks all named 'Twin Sisters Olivine Scramble'. The name identifies a rock type and a range, not a climb, so on a route list these three rows are indistinguishable from one another and from the North and South Twin scramble rows nearby. Worth renaming per peak.
_DEFECTS.little_sister_scramble_carries_the_west_: wa_little_sister_scramble's fa field reads 'Darin Berdinka, June 21, 2013 (West Face)' — the same party and date as wa_little_sister_west_face. Either the scramble row has borrowed a neighbouring route's first ascent, or the two rows are the same climb. Its aspect column (S/SE) also disagrees with its own approach and climbing_route prose, both of which describe gaining and following the WEST ridge.
_DEFECTS.little_sister_high_point_disagrees_betwe: wa_little_sister_scramble gives high_point_ft 6,536 while wa_little_sister_north_face, wa_little_sister_south_couloir, wa_little_sister_southeast_ridge and wa_little_sister_west_face all give 6,600 for the same summit.
_DEFECTS.skookum_approach_conflates_two_different: wa_skookum_peak_twinsisters_scramble's approach has the Green Creek climbers' path leaving Elbow Lake Trail #697 at Elbow Lake, about 8 miles in. Every other route in the same basin — and every source consulted — puts that junction at a switchback near Hildebrand Creek around 2,600 ft, roughly 1.5 miles in. The row also reaches Skookum from the Green Creek cirque, while circuit accounts gain its north ridge by dropping off South Twin's southwest side.
_DEFECTS.goat_mountain_south_ridge_high_point_dis: wa_goat_mountain_south_ridge stores high_point_ft 6,721 while its own approach and climbing_route prose repeatedly name the true East summit as 6,892 ft. The sibling row wa_goat_mountain_east_peak stores 6,891 for the same summit. One of the two Goat Mountain rows is 170 ft short.
_DEFECTS.herman_high_point_disagrees_with_its_own: wa_mount_herman_standard_scramble stores high_point_ft 6,240 while its approach and climbing_route prose both name the true summit as 6,285 ft.
_DEFECTS.baker_boulder_camp_elevation_disagrees_b: wa_mount_baker_boulder_glacier puts the ridge high camp 'around 5,500 ft'; wa_mount_baker_boulder_park_cleaver puts it 'around 5,700 ft'. The two rows share a trailhead, a trail and the same camp, and describe it 200 ft apart.
_DEFECTS.baker_boulder_glacier_fa_field_documents: wa_mount_baker_boulder_glacier's fa field says the 1894 Morovits ascent 'instead established the adjacent Boulder-Park Cleaver ridge route, a different line on the same mountain'. That is a note ABOUT the neighbouring row stored in this row's first-ascent field, and wa_mount_baker_boulder_park_cleaver duly carries Morovits and the same date. The fa column is a value, not a place for a disambiguation paragraph.
_DEFECTS.shuksan_hanging_glacier_bivy_elevation_d: wa_mount_shuksan_hanging_glacier's approach puts the bivy 'around 6,000-6,500 ft, below the first rock/ice barrier', and then puts the base of the technical climbing at 'roughly 7,500-8,000 ft'. The Mountaineers' route description for the same ground puts the good bivy sites at 5,500 ft where the ridge meets the North Face. That is a spread of a thousand feet on the one number a party plans its day around. No figure was carried into the variants; the arrival is described by feature instead.
_DEFECTS.shuksan_northeast_ridge_trailhead_coordi: wa_mount_shuksan_northeast_ridge's approach_logistics names the 'White Salmon Day-Lodge area (FR-3075, Mt. Baker Ski Area)' but stores trailheadLat/Lng 48.8595 / -121.648. wa_mount_shuksan_northwest_arete stores the identical pair for a trailhead it calls the 'White Salmon Road (hairpin) TH / Lower White Salmon Lodge'. Two different named trailheads, one coordinate — the audit:trailhead-agreement shape, between rows rather than within one.
_DEFECTS.truncated_trailhead_directions: EIGHT rows in this batch store an approach_logistics.trailheadDirection that has been cut mid-sentence, in every case at the abbreviation 'Mt.' or 'elev.' — the string appears to have been split on a full stop. Verified against the live rows: wa_hadley_peak_cougar_divide and wa_hadley_peak_skyline_divide both read 'From Glacier, WA, drive Mt.'; wa_mount_sefrit_southwest_ridge reads 'From Glacier, drive Mt.'; wa_the_pleiades_scramble reads 'From Glacier, WA, drive east about 12 miles on SR 542 (Mt.'; wa_table_mountain_standard_scramble reads 'From the Artist Point trailhead (elev.'; wa_winchester_mountain_south_trail reads 'From the Twin Lakes trailhead (elev.'; wa_mount_herman_standard_scramble reads 'Start from the Bagley Lakes Trailhead (~4,200 ft) at the south end of the upper Mt.'; and wa_ruth_mountain_south_slopes reads 'From the Hannegan Pass Trailhead (end of FR-32, ~5.3 miles off Mt.'. Every one is a user-facing directions string that stops before it says where to go. The tell is the abbreviation, so this is a splitter that treats '.' as a sentence end, not a length cap.
_DEFECTS.ruth_icy_traverse_stores_a_paragraph_in_: wa_ruth_icy_traverse's approach_logistics.trailheadDirection holds 240 characters of route prose beginning 'Shares its trailhead and lower approach with the South Slopes/Ruth Glacier route...' and ending mid-sentence at 'then '. Same column, opposite failure from the truncations above: too much prose rather than too little.
_DEFECTS.ruth_mountain_row_still_named_for_the_wr: The row id wa_ruth_mountain_south_slopes still encodes 'south slopes' although the row's name column now correctly reads 'North Face / Ruth Glacier' and its aspect is N. The rename has landed on the name and not on the id, so a session grepping by id will still be told this is a south-side climb.
_DEFECTS.sefrits_two_ruth_creek_routes_carry_the_: wa_mount_sefrit_southeast_ridge and wa_mount_sefrit_bloody_head_couloir both store trailheadLat/Lng 48.91049444 / -121.5894222 — the identical pair that wa_ruth_mountain_south_slopes and wa_ruth_icy_traverse store for the Hannegan Pass Trailhead at the end of FR-32, where it is correct. Neither Sefrit route starts there: the Southeast Ridge's own approach puts its start at the Ruth Creek Road pullout near milepost 3 at about 2,950 ft, and Bloody Head leaves the Ruth Creek trail at about 3,450 ft. Both rows say so in their own prose while their coordinates point at the road end. The Southeast Ridge row also disagrees with itself: its trailheadDirection says 'Hannegan Campground pullout at the END of Ruth Creek Road' while its approach says milepost 3.
_DEFECTS.fourteen_rows_carry_a_trailhead_name_wit: Verified against the live rows: wa_hadley_peak_cougar_divide, wa_hadley_peak_skyline_divide, wa_goat_mountain_south_ridge, wa_north_twin_sister_scramble, wa_north_twin_sister_west_ridge, wa_south_twin_sister_north_ridge, wa_south_twin_sister_scramble, wa_south_twin_sister_west_ridge, wa_skookum_peak_twinsisters_scramble, wa_cinderella_peak_scramble, wa_tomyhoi_peak_southeast_ridge, wa_the_pleiades_scramble, wa_mount_herman_standard_scramble and wa_table_mountain_standard_scramble all store a trailhead NAME with absent trailheadLat/trailheadLng. Fourteen rows in one region with no machine-readable start point — which also means audit:trailhead-agreement has nothing to compare against on any of them.
_DEFECTS.two_rows_carry_no_high_point_at_all: wa_mount_sefrit_bloody_head_couloir and wa_mount_shuksan_northwest_arete both store high_point_ft null, while their sibling rows on the same peaks carry 7,191 and 9,131 respectively.
_DEFECTS.goat_mountain_east_peak_row_has_no_appro: wa_goat_mountain_east_peak carries an approach paragraph but no approach_logistics object — no trailhead name, no coordinate, no direction. Its sibling wa_goat_mountain_south_ridge has one.
_DEFECTS.little_sister_southeast_ridge_row_has_no: wa_little_sister_southeast_ridge has an approach paragraph and no approach_logistics object, while the other four Little Sister rows all carry the same Elbow Lake Trailhead block.
_DEFECTS.canadian_border_peak_and_church_mountain: Three places named in the scope for this batch do not exist in the catalog. Canadian Border Peak is correct to be absent — it is in British Columbia. Church Mountain is a real Mount Baker Highway peak with a lookout and a maintained trail and has no area row and no routes. Yellow Aster Butte has no area of its own; the trailhead named for it serves the Tomyhoi Peak route.
_DEFECTS.american_border_peak_northeast_face_is_a: wa_american_border_peak_northeast_face holds a name, an aspect (NE), a season and a high point. It has no grade, no pitches, no fa, no approach, no approach_logistics, no descent and no beta. It is a placeholder rather than a route, and it sits on a peak whose near-twin across the international border does have north-side beta — which is exactly how a Canadian route would end up filed on a Washington peak.
